findings.description: Exclusion of individuals living in the same household as an enrolled participant may reduce representativeness and introduce subtle socio-demographic bias.
findings.recommendation: Reconsider same-household exclusion or provide strong justification; monitor for recruitment imbalances by socioeconomic status.
findings.actual_outcome: Impact on generalisability is uncertain but may have reduced inclusion of certain household structures.

findings.type: Diabetes exclusion limits generalizability to real-world hypertension population
findings.description: Exclusion of participants with diabetes produces a cleaner pathophysiological sample but limits applicability to the large proportion of hypertensive patients with coexisting diabetes.
findings.recommendation: Explicitly position trial as non-diabetic high-risk hypertension population; plan complementary studies including diabetes.
findings.actual_outcome: SPRINT results cannot be directly extrapolated to patients with both diabetes and hypertension.

findings.description: BP measurement protocol is not described with sufficient operational detail; automated vs manual, attended vs unattended procedures are not fully standardised or clearly documented.
findings.recommendation: Add explicit BP measurement protocol including device type, calibration, number of readings, rest period, attended vs unattended conditions, and site training requirements.
findings.actual_outcome: Post-publication controversy: SPRINT BP values may be systematically lower than routine clinic measurements, complicating translation of the "120 mmHg" target to real-world practice.

findings.type: Unintentional weight loss exclusion operationally vague
findings.description: Exclusion based on "unintentional weight loss" lacks a quantitative definition (e.g. % body weight over time), leaving room for variable site interpretation.
findings.recommendation: Define unintentional weight loss with quantitative thresholds (e.g. >5% body weight over 6–12 months) and standardised assessment methods.
findings.actual_outcome: Site-to-site variability in interpretation; some at-risk participants may have been included or excluded inconsistently.

findings.description: Chronic kidney disease subgroup is of high interest, but event rates and sample size may be insufficient for robust conclusions on renal outcomes.
findings.recommendation: Pre-specify realistic renal endpoint analyses with appropriate caution about power; consider extended follow-up or pooled analyses.
findings.actual_outcome: Published SPRINT results showed limited power to detect differences in some renal outcomes.

findings.type: MIND substudy consent and eligibility process ambiguous
findings.description: The process for consent and eligibility in the cognitive substudy (MIND) is not fully integrated with the main protocol text.
findings.recommendation: Provide a clear cross-reference and flow diagram showing which participants are eligible and how consent for MIND is obtained.
findings.actual_outcome: Primarily affects clarity of substudy processes rather than main trial validity.

findings.type: Adaptive sample size stopping rules not operationalized
findings.description: Mentions of potential adaptive features or early stopping are not fully formalised into statistical decision rules.
findings.recommendation: If adaptive elements are planned, specify formal statistical boundaries and DSMB decision criteria; otherwise, remove ambiguous references.
findings.actual_outcome: Ambiguity may confuse interpretation of early stopping decisions and perceived robustness of results.
